blocks.orig: Many of the Serengeti antelopes will be familiar to visitors from books, television or movies.
blocks.html: Visitors will already know many of the Serengeti antelopes from books, television or films.

blocks.orig: But there are a great number of antelope that perhaps are not so famous or familiar although just as important to the ecology of the landscape.
blocks.html: Yet there are also plenty of antelope that are less famous or familiar, even though they matter just as much to the ecology of the landscape.

blocks.orig: We take a look at the antelopes of the Serengeti as part of a safari guide to Tanzania and list all the wonderful animals you shouldn’t miss while visiting this beautiful part of Africa.
blocks.html: As part of our safari guide to Tanzania, we look at the antelopes of the Serengeti and list all the wonderful animals you should not miss when you visit this beautiful part of Africa.

blocks.orig: The Serengeti National Park is more than 14,750 square kilometers and home to 300 mammal species. In fact the park is most famous for its large herds of plains animals.
blocks.html: Covering more than 14,750 square kilometers, the Serengeti National Park is home to 300 species of mammal. The park is best known for its large herds of plains animals.

blocks.orig: Among these are the different types of antelope which live in different parts of the Serengeti.
blocks.html: They include the various types of antelope that live in different parts of the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: From the large wildebeest and eland to the tiny dik-dik and klipspringer this area of Africa has a wide range of wonderful antelope, sixteen types in total.
blocks.html: This part of Africa has a wide variety of wonderful antelope, sixteen types altogether, ranging from the large wildebeest and eland to the tiny dik-dik and klipspringer.

blocks.orig: Some are incredibly pretty and others are just downright tough. Yet this incredible diversity of antelope all live in the same area, albeit quite a large area.
blocks.html: Some of them are remarkably pretty, while others are simply tough. Even so, this incredible variety of antelope all share the same area, admittedly a fairly large one.

blocks.orig: So, let’s take a look at these incredible Serengeti antelopes.
blocks.html: Let’s have a closer look at these incredible Serengeti antelopes.

blocks.orig: Wildebeest are perhaps the most well known of the antelope on the Serengeti. It is one of the largest antelope and is also known as the gnu, blue wildebeest or brindled gnu.
blocks.html: Of all the antelope on the Serengeti, the wildebeest is probably the best known. It ranks among the largest antelope and is also called the gnu, blue wildebeest or brindled gnu.

blocks.orig: The are most famous for their massive numbers that take part in the Great Migration. This is when millions of large animals move in a large circular path following food and water sources.
blocks.html: They are best known for the huge numbers that join the Great Migration, when millions of large animals travel in a wide circular route in search of food and water.

blocks.orig: The wildebeest while making up a large part of this migration but are not the only participants.
blocks.html: Although wildebeest make up a large share of this migration, they are not the only animals taking part.

blocks.orig: These large antelope are herbivores meaning they graze on vegetation such as grass and leaves.
blocks.html: These large antelope are herbivores, which means they feed on plants such as grass and leaves.

blocks.orig: They have a long rectangular head and a mane that extends down the ridge on their back.
blocks.html: Their head is long and rectangular, and a mane runs down the ridge of their back.

blocks.orig: Both the male and female wildebeest have long curved horns though the males tend to be bigger with a slightly darker coat.
blocks.html: Male and female wildebeest both have long, curved horns, although the males are usually larger and have a slightly darker coat.

blocks.orig: Subspecies vary in color from slate gray to dark brown.
blocks.html: Colour differs by subspecies, from slate gray to dark brown.

blocks.orig: The eland are very large antelope and can weigh up to 2,000 pounds with a shoulder height of around 4.9 feet. Males tend to be bigger than females.
blocks.html: Eland are very large antelope, weighing up to 2,000 pounds and standing around 4.9 feet at the shoulder. The males are usually larger than the females.

blocks.orig: One of the most distinguishing features of the eland is their spiral horns.
blocks.html: Their spiral horns are among the most recognisable features of the eland.

blocks.orig: They also have a prominent black stripe which runs down the center of their back and dewlaps under their neck. These help with thermoregulation in arid climates.
blocks.html: A prominent black stripe also runs down the middle of their back, and they have dewlaps beneath the neck, which help them regulate their temperature in dry climates.

blocks.orig: Elands are known as ‘track on track’ walkers.
blocks.html: Eland are described as ‘track on track’ walkers.

blocks.orig: This means wherever a front foot lands the rear foot will land in the same spot to minimize the amount of noise they make walking in the bush.
blocks.html: In other words, the rear foot lands exactly where the front foot touched down, so they make as little noise as possible when moving through the bush.

blocks.orig: They can jump over three meters in height and can survive in desert, mountain or bush habitats. Eland are found in the northern woodlands of the Serengeti during the dry season.
blocks.html: They can leap more than three meters high and are able to survive in desert, mountain or bush habitats. In the dry season you will find eland in the northern woodlands of the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: In the wet season they are more often found in the southern or eastern plains of the park.
blocks.html: During the wet season they are more likely to be in the southern or eastern plains of the park.

blocks.orig: This Serengeti antelope is a striking creature and quite easy to identify. Although you may have a hard time spotting them as they are very shy and spend most of their time in thick vegetation.
blocks.html: This Serengeti antelope is a striking animal and fairly easy to recognise. Spotting one can be tricky, though, because they are very shy and spend most of their time in dense vegetation.

blocks.orig: Males have spiral horns and are typically larger than the females.
blocks.html: The males have spiral horns and are usually bigger than the females.

blocks.orig: They have thin white stripes across their bodies and down the back with two thicker white stripes on the throat and neck. Males have a dark brown coat while females are more reddish brown.
blocks.html: Thin white stripes run across their bodies and down their backs, with two broader white stripes on the throat and neck. The males’ coat is dark brown, while the females are a more reddish brown.

blocks.orig: Lesser kudu spend most of their time in the forests of the southwestern Serengeti.
blocks.html: The lesser kudu spends most of its time in the forests of the southwestern Serengeti.

blocks.orig: Being quite difficult to see you are more likely to spot a flash of white from under their tail as they move away from you.
blocks.html: Because they are hard to see, you are more likely to catch a flash of white from beneath their tail as they move away from you.

blocks.orig: To distinguish between them from the greater kudu the legs and horns of the lesser kudu have an orange tinge to them.
blocks.html: You can tell the lesser kudu apart from the greater kudu by the orange tinge on its legs and horns.

blocks.orig: Bohor reedbuck are commonly spotted close to water sources in the Serengeti, mainly hiding in the tall grass. They are a medium sized antelope with long limbs.
blocks.html: In the Serengeti, Bohor reedbuck are often seen near water, usually hidden in the tall grass. They are medium-sized antelope with long legs.

blocks.orig: Rams have stouter necks and build than females. They also have small, forward-facing horns while the females have none.
blocks.html: Rams are more solidly built than females and have thicker necks. They also carry small horns that point forwards, whereas females have none.

blocks.orig: The coat is a yellow to grayish brown color with white undersides, and they have a dark stripe on the front of each foreleg.
blocks.html: Their coat ranges from yellow to grayish brown with white undersides, and there is a dark stripe on the front of each foreleg.

blocks.orig: Males can reach between 100-133 lbs while females are smaller at 77-100 lbs.
blocks.html: Males weigh between 100-133 lbs, while the smaller females weigh 77-100 lbs.

blocks.orig: Bohor reedbuck live in small groups or pairs, and they are predominantly nocturnal, preferring to graze at night.
blocks.html: Bohor reedbuck live in pairs or small groups and are mostly nocturnal, preferring to graze after dark.

blocks.orig: Females give birth to a single calf after a gestation period of over 7 months.
blocks.html: After a gestation of more than 7 months, the female gives birth to a single calf.

blocks.orig: The young hide for the first two to three months of their life only coming out to nurse for 10-30 minutes at a time.
blocks.html: For the first two to three months the young stay hidden, emerging only to nurse for 10-30 minutes at a time.

blocks.orig: East African oryx also known as beisa are a threatened species of the Serengeti, with populations declining.
blocks.html: The East African oryx, also called beisa, is a threatened species in the Serengeti, and its numbers are falling.

blocks.orig: These animals have been illegally hunted by those who believe their blood and flesh can cure illnesses or give extraordinary strength.
blocks.html: They have been hunted illegally by people who believe that their blood and meat can cure illness or give exceptional strength.

blocks.orig: The subspecies fringe-eared oryx is the type found in the Serengeti.
blocks.html: In the Serengeti, the subspecies you will find is the fringe-eared oryx.

blocks.orig: It is a very distinctive type of Serengeti antelope, fawn in color with black bands and white stripes on its face. There is a black line on the body where the fawn color gives way to a white underbelly.
blocks.html: This Serengeti antelope is very distinctive: fawn in colour, with black bands and white stripes on its face. A black line marks the point on its body where the fawn colouring changes to a white belly.

blocks.orig: Males and females tend to look the same, both having long, straight horns which have a ringed appearance.
blocks.html: Males and females look much alike, and both have long, straight horns with a ringed appearance.

blocks.orig: They are a territorial animal and will use their speed as a defense mechanism against predators.
blocks.html: They are territorial animals and rely on their speed to defend themselves against predators.

blocks.orig: This is a beautiful antelope, quite often confused with the more widely known Thomson’s gazelle.
blocks.html: This lovely antelope is often mistaken for the better-known Thomson’s gazelle.

blocks.orig: The Grant’s gazelle is however, larger and doesn’t have the black stripe on its side. They also have a white patch on the tail that extends up their back.
blocks.html: The Grant’s gazelle, however, is bigger and lacks the black stripe along its side. It also has a white patch on the tail that runs up its back.

blocks.orig: These Serengeti antelope live in large herds and take part in the Great Migration each year. They can go long periods without water.
blocks.html: These Serengeti antelope live in large herds and join the Great Migration every year. They can manage for long periods without water.

blocks.orig: This is possible as they have the ability to raise their body temperature so that they sweat less when they are hot, thereby conserving water.
blocks.html: They can do this because they are able to let their body temperature rise, so they sweat less in the heat and save water.

blocks.orig: Male Grant’s gazelles weigh between 121-176 lbs and females between 77-100 lbs.
blocks.html: Male Grant’s gazelles weigh 121-176 lbs and females 77-100 lbs.

blocks.orig: Both the male and female have lyre-shaped horns which have a ringed appearance. They can measure between 18-30 inches in length.
blocks.html: Males and females both carry lyre-shaped horns with a ringed appearance, measuring 18-30 inches in length.

blocks.orig: Females give birth to one calf after a 7-month gestation. The calf is kept hidden in long grass, and the mother leaves to graze, returning several times a day to nurse the baby gazelle.
blocks.html: After a gestation of 7 months, the female gives birth to one calf. She keeps the calf hidden in the long grass and goes off to graze, coming back several times a day to feed the young gazelle.

blocks.orig: One of the better known antelopes of the Serengeti is the Thomson’s gazelle.
blocks.html: The Thomson’s gazelle is one of the better-known antelopes of the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: Smaller than its counterpart, the Grant’s gazelle, it has a distinctive lateral stripe on its abdomen to further tell them apart.
blocks.html: It is smaller than its relative, the Grant’s gazelle, and a distinctive stripe along the side of its belly helps to tell the two apart.

blocks.orig: There are two subspecies of Thomson’s gazelles, the eastern and Serengeti Thomson’s gazelle.
blocks.html: Thomson’s gazelles come in two subspecies: the eastern and the Serengeti Thomson’s gazelle.

blocks.orig: The variety found in the Serengeti has a whiter face than the eastern gazelle and a black stripe which goes from the inner eye to the mouth.
blocks.html: The type found in the Serengeti has a whiter face than the eastern gazelle, plus a black stripe running from the inner corner of the eye to the mouth.

blocks.orig: It is estimated that there are around 500,000 gazelles in the Serengeti, a mixture of Thomson’s and Grant’s gazelles.
blocks.html: Around 500,000 gazelles are estimated to live in the Serengeti, a mix of Thomson’s and Grant’s gazelles.

blocks.orig: This makes them the second most numerous antelope in the park after the wildebeest.
blocks.html: That makes them the second most numerous antelope in the park, after the wildebeest.

blocks.orig: Female Thomson’s gazelles have shorter horns than the males.
blocks.html: The horns of female Thomson’s gazelles are shorter than those of the males.

blocks.orig: They give birth to a single calf following a 6-month gestation. Young Thomson’s gazelles often fall prey to predators in calving season.
blocks.html: After a gestation of 6 months they give birth to a single calf. During calving season, young Thomson’s gazelles are often taken by predators.

blocks.orig: The waterbuck as its name suggests tends to stay close to a water source and needs a good supply of grass to feed.
blocks.html: As the name suggests, the waterbuck usually stays near water, and it needs plenty of grass to eat.

blocks.orig: For this reason it has very specific regions of the Serengeti where it lives such as the woodlands in the central part of the park.
blocks.html: That is why it lives only in quite specific parts of the Serengeti, such as the woodlands in the centre of the park.

blocks.orig: These antelopes of the Serengeti are quite easy to identify as they have long, shaggy hair on their neck and a white ring on their rump.
blocks.html: These Serengeti antelopes are fairly easy to recognise, thanks to the long, shaggy hair on their neck and the white ring on their rump.

blocks.orig: Their coat has a water repellent layer thanks to a coating of oil and the males’ long, sweeping horns are faintly ringed. Horn length can be up to 40 inches.
blocks.html: An oily coating makes their coat water-repellent, and the males’ long, sweeping horns are lightly ringed, reaching up to 40 inches in length.

blocks.orig: Waterbuck are not a common prey for large predators which may be due to their thick coat. Perhaps for this reason they are typically only attacked by very hungry lions.
blocks.html: Large predators rarely hunt waterbuck, possibly because of their thick coat. This may be why usually only very hungry lions attack them.

blocks.orig: Male waterbuck are usually about 25% larger than females.
blocks.html: Male waterbuck are generally about 25% bigger than the females.

blocks.orig: Breeding season can be spread throughout the year and there is a high mortality rate of young due to predators such as big cats.
blocks.html: Breeding can take place at any time of year, and many young die because of predators such as big cats.

blocks.orig: Hartebeests are also known as kongoni or kaama.
blocks.html: Hartebeests are also called kongoni or kaama.

blocks.orig: Despite their large size and ungainly appearance the hartebeest is one of the fastest antelope, capable of reaching 43 miles an hour. They are also surprisingly elegant for such a large mammal.
blocks.html: Although it is large and looks rather awkward, the hartebeest is among the fastest antelope and can reach 43 miles an hour. For such a big mammal it is also surprisingly elegant.

blocks.orig: These Serengeti antelope are quite easily recognizable with their long faces, and steeply sloping backs.
blocks.html: These Serengeti antelope are easy to recognise by their long faces and sharply sloping backs.

blocks.orig: They also have wide sweeping horns as opposed to the more common parallel horns of other antelope.
blocks.html: Their horns also sweep out widely, unlike the parallel horns that are more common in other antelope.

blocks.orig: Their name actually translates to ‘tough ox’ and they are certainly resilient.
blocks.html: The name in fact means ‘tough ox’, and they are certainly hardy.

blocks.orig: Hartebeests are not picky eaters and will eat what is available. Females will however, only give birth when there is availability of food.
blocks.html: Hartebeests are not fussy and will eat whatever they can find. Females, however, only give birth when food is available.

blocks.orig: Hartebeest stand at around 3-5 feet at the shoulder and weigh between 165-440 pounds. They live in organized herds which can exceed 300 animals.
blocks.html: Hartebeest measure around 3-5 feet at the shoulder and weigh 165-440 pounds. They live in organised herds that can number more than 300 animals.

blocks.orig: These small antelope are adorable and their behavior as well as their cute appearance will endear them to most people.
blocks.html: These small antelope are adorable, and most people will be charmed by both their behaviour and their cute looks.

blocks.orig: Despite their fragile appearance these are hardy animals who live in mountainous areas of the Serengeti and often in extremes of temperature.
blocks.html: They may look fragile, but these are hardy animals that live in the mountainous parts of the Serengeti, often in extreme temperatures.

blocks.orig: Klipspringers eat a wide variety of grass and plants from which they derive most of their water requirements.
blocks.html: Klipspringers feed on a wide range of grasses and plants, which provide most of the water they need.

blocks.orig: Like other dwarf antelope such as the dik-dik they form monogamous pairs, and defend their territory together.
blocks.html: Like other dwarf antelope, such as the dik-dik, they live in monogamous pairs and defend their territory together.

blocks.orig: Males are particularly vigilant and stand guard for extended periods to protect the pair’s territory and young. This leaves the female to tend to the single calf.
blocks.html: The males are especially watchful and keep guard for long periods to protect the pair’s territory and young, leaving the female to look after the single calf.

blocks.orig: Young klipspringers are kept hidden for 2-3 months from predators such as eagles and leave the parents at a year old.
blocks.html: Young klipspringers stay hidden from predators such as eagles for 2-3 months and leave their parents when they are a year old.

blocks.orig: The bushbuck is an elusive and shy Serengeti antelope which spends most of its time in thick vegetation.
blocks.html: The bushbuck is a shy, elusive Serengeti antelope that spends most of its time in dense vegetation.

blocks.orig: However, it has white patches on its ears, legs, tail, chin and neck which are the most mobile parts of its body. So you may catch a glimpse of one if you’re lucky.
blocks.html: It does, however, have white patches on its ears, legs, tail, chin and neck, the parts of its body that move the most. With a bit of luck, you may get a glimpse of one.

blocks.orig: Males have large spiral horns which can be between 10-20 inches long. They are not territorial and are very solitary.
blocks.html: The males carry large spiral horns measuring 10-20 inches. They are not territorial and live very solitary lives.

blocks.orig: Females don’t have horns and also have very different pelage or fur. While the male’s coat is dark gray the female’s is reddish brown with more white spots all over the body.
blocks.html: Females have no horns, and their pelage, or fur, is quite different too. The male’s coat is dark gray, whereas the female’s is reddish brown with more white spots across the body.

blocks.orig: The biggest threat to the bushbuck is the loss of its habitat as humans encroach on where it lives with roads, agriculture and settlements.
blocks.html: The greatest threat to the bushbuck is habitat loss, as people move into the areas where it lives with roads, farming and settlements.

blocks.orig: Impala are another well known antelope from the Serengeti and one of the most abundant.
blocks.html: The impala is another familiar antelope of the Serengeti, and one of the most plentiful.

blocks.orig: They are mid-sized and very graceful with an easily recognizable face, having a white spot above their eyes. They also have a black stripe down the middle of their tail.
blocks.html: Medium-sized and very graceful, they have an easily recognised face with a white spot above the eyes. A black stripe also runs down the centre of their tail.

blocks.orig: Males have lyre-shaped horns with a distinctive ringed appearance, females have no horns. Impala are extremely fast runners and agile jumpers both of which they use to evade predators.
blocks.html: The males have lyre-shaped horns with a distinctive ringed look, while the females have none. Impala are very fast runners and nimble jumpers, and they use both skills to escape predators.

blocks.orig: Average height to the shoulder is between 28-36 inches and weight is 88-165 pounds. They move around in breeding herds with a territorial male shepherding the females.
blocks.html: On average they stand 28-36 inches at the shoulder and weigh 88-165 pounds. They travel in breeding herds, with a territorial male keeping the females together.

blocks.orig: Females give birth to a single calf which only remains in hiding for a couple of days before joining the creche of other young impala.
blocks.html: The female gives birth to a single calf, which stays hidden for only a couple of days before joining a creche of other young impala.

blocks.orig: In the northern parts of the Serengeti you will find the oribi, a small slender antelope with reddish brown fur or pelage and a white underside.
blocks.html: The oribi lives in the northern parts of the Serengeti. It is a small, slender antelope with reddish brown fur, or pelage, and a white underside.

blocks.orig: It can be easily identified by the dark spot or sweat gland under its ears.
blocks.html: The dark spot, or sweat gland, below its ears makes it easy to identify.

blocks.orig: Male oribis have small, sharp horns that are completely straight, the females do not have horns. They are actually a type of dwarf antelope with a long neck and long legs so look almost gazelle-like.
blocks.html: Male oribis carry small, sharp horns that are perfectly straight, while the females have none. They are in fact a kind of dwarf antelope, and with their long neck and long legs they look almost like a gazelle.

blocks.orig: These antelope live in pairs or small herds but have the lowest distribution across the Serengeti so if you happen to see some consider yourself lucky.
blocks.html: They live in pairs or small herds, but they are the least widely distributed antelope in the Serengeti, so you can count yourself lucky if you see some.

blocks.orig: Females are slightly larger than the males and are between 20-30 inches tall. Average weight is about 31 pounds.
blocks.html: The females are a little larger than the males, standing 20-30 inches tall. They weigh about 31 pounds on average.

blocks.orig: Steenboks are another small antelope which can be seen around the woodlands of the southwestern Serengeti and in some parts of the north.
blocks.html: The steenbok is another small antelope, found in the woodlands of the southwestern Serengeti and in parts of the north.

blocks.orig: They are an extremely pretty antelope with large eyes and ears.
blocks.html: With their large eyes and ears, they are a very pretty antelope.

blocks.orig: Their coat is a fawn color with an orange tinge, and they have a distinctive teardrop shaped black patch above their nose.
blocks.html: Their fawn coat has an orange tinge, and a distinctive black patch shaped like a teardrop sits above the nose.

blocks.orig: Steenboks feed on young plants, foliage and leaves and can wander far from water sources.
blocks.html: Steenboks eat young plants, foliage and leaves, and they can roam a long way from water.

blocks.orig: When threatened by a predator, steenboks will run in a zig-zag pattern to try and confuse or throw off their pursuer. They are normally found in the shade during the hottest part of the day.
blocks.html: If a predator threatens them, steenboks run in a zig-zag to confuse or shake off whatever is chasing them. In the hottest part of the day they usually stay in the shade.

blocks.orig: Male steenbok have a pair of menacingly sharp horns. The females have none but are larger than the males.
blocks.html: Male steenbok carry a pair of menacingly sharp horns. Females have none, but they are bigger than the males.

blocks.orig: These dainty little antelope are very cute and are widespread across the Serengeti. They are normally found in thick vegetation where they may be hard to see due to their size.
blocks.html: These delicate little antelope are very cute and occur throughout the Serengeti. They usually stay in dense vegetation, where their small size can make them hard to spot.

blocks.orig: In fact, they are the smallest antelope in the Serengeti at only 12-16 inches high.
blocks.html: Standing just 12-16 inches high, they are in fact the smallest antelope in the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: Dik-dik are fairly sedentary but if needed can run up to 26 miles per hour.
blocks.html: Dik-dik tend to stay in one place, but they can run at up to 26 miles per hour when they have to.

blocks.orig: When a predator approaches the female’s alarm call is a ‘dik-dik’ sound from which they got their name. Pairs mate for life.
blocks.html: When a predator comes close, the female gives an alarm call that sounds like ‘dik-dik’, which is where their name comes from. Pairs stay together for life.

blocks.orig: Males have small horns which are often concealed by the small tuft of hair on their head. They have large eyes which are surrounded by a ring of white fur, making them stand out.
blocks.html: The males have small horns that are often hidden by the little tuft of hair on their head. Their large eyes are ringed with white fur, which makes them stand out.

blocks.orig: Below each eye is a scent marking gland.
blocks.html: Beneath each eye is a gland used for scent marking.

blocks.orig: Topi bear a striking resemblance to the hartebeest, this is because they belong to the same sub-family.
blocks.html: Topi look strikingly like the hartebeest, because the two belong to the same sub-family.

blocks.orig: They both have short necks, long legs and long faces, but the topi is darker on the top of the legs. Medium in size the topi has a reddish brown coat.
blocks.html: Both have short necks, long legs and long faces, although the topi is darker on the upper legs. The topi is medium-sized with a reddish brown coat.

blocks.orig: These are a very social antelope and can be seen in great numbers on the plains of the eastern Serengeti.
blocks.html: These antelope are very sociable and gather in large numbers on the plains of the eastern Serengeti.

blocks.orig: The males shepherd groups of females, but their social organization is quite flexible.
blocks.html: Males keep groups of females together, though their social structure is fairly flexible.

blocks.orig: Similarly flexible are their breeding habits. Normally calving only happens once a year but if food is plentiful they will calve more than once. If a female senses danger she can delay the labor process.
blocks.html: Their breeding is just as flexible. Calving usually happens once a year, but when food is abundant they will calve more than once. If a female senses danger, she can postpone giving birth.

blocks.orig: The gerenuk is a tall, elegant antelope which closely resembles a gazelle. It has a long, slender neck and limbs. All of these features explain why it is also called the giraffe gazelle.
blocks.html: The gerenuk is a tall, elegant antelope that looks very much like a gazelle. Its neck and legs are long and slender, which explains why it is also known as the giraffe gazelle.

blocks.orig: A flat wedge shaped head and large, round eyes add to the beauty of this graceful Serengeti antelope.
blocks.html: Its flat, wedge-shaped head and large, round eyes add to the beauty of this graceful Serengeti antelope.

blocks.orig: Male gerenuk stand at approximately 35-41 inches tall and the females are slightly shorter at an average of 31-39 inches.
blocks.html: Male gerenuk are about 35-41 inches tall, while the females are a little shorter at an average of 31-39 inches.

blocks.orig: A male weighs anything between 68-115 pounds while the smaller females average between 62-99 pounds.
blocks.html: Males weigh anywhere from 68-115 pounds, and the smaller females average 62-99 pounds.

blocks.orig: In terms of coloration the gerenuk has a reddish brown back and lighter, fawn to buff colored flanks. The insides of the legs and the underside of the belly are a cream color and the eyes and mouth are surrounded by white fur.
blocks.html: As for colouring, the gerenuk has a reddish brown back with paler flanks in fawn to buff. The inner legs and the belly are cream, and white fur surrounds the eyes and mouth.

blocks.orig: Female gerenuk have a distinctive dark patch on the crown and the males have lyre shaped horns. Mainly active during the day the gerenuk may be spotted shading from the noon sun or feeding on foliage.
blocks.html: Female gerenuk have a distinctive dark patch on top of the head, and the males carry lyre-shaped horns. The gerenuk is mostly active during the day, and you may see it sheltering from the midday sun or browsing on foliage.
